Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 2576 of 2021

Appellant :- Ranvir @ Putan
Respondent :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Appellant :- Kumar Beenu Singh,Sanjeev Kumar Sharma Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra,J.
Order on Bail Application Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned AGA for the State.

As this appeal arises out of impugned judgement and order dated 12.02.2021 passed by Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (NDPS Act), Court no. 7, Ramabai Nagar (Kanpur Dehat) in Session Trial No. 203 of 2016 (State vs. Ranvir @ Puttan and others), in Case Crime no. 63 of 2016, under Sections 498A, 304B, 201 IPC and Section 4 of D.P. Act, P.S. Ghatampur, District Kanpur Nagar,
convicting the appellant under Section 304-B IPC and sentencing him to undergo ten years imprisonment with fine of Rs. 10,000/-; under Section 498-A IPC, three years imprisonment with fine of Rs. 5,000/- and under Section 4 of D.P. Act, six month imprisonment with fine of Rs. 1,000/-
with default stipulation; the bail application of the appellant is being disposed of by this order:
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that according to prosecution version,
F.I.R. in the present case was lodged by the informant, who is uncle of the deceased Smt. Bitola on 10.1.2016 under Sections 498-A, 304-B IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P.
Act against present appellant, who is husband of the deceased and four others, who Ranvir @ Putan vs State Of U.P. on 16 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113159440/
1 are his family members with allegation that deceased died within four years of her marriage and her mud stained dead body was found in a wheat field of the village of her in-laws on 7.1.2016, she was killed by her husband and in-laws in the night of 6.1.2016 and dead body was thrown in the field.

sentences.text:
He next submitted that co-accused Arvind Yadav, Smt. Mithlesh and Pankaj, who are family members of the appellant and are assigned similar role in the offence, are already enlarged on bail vide order dated 18.3.2021 passed by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Appeal No.
1223 of 2021.

He next submitted that appellant and his family members have been implicated in the offence on the basis of suspicion and there is no proximate live link between cruelty allegedly practiced against the deceased and her death.
There is no clinching and unimpeachable evidence on record to prove the commission of offence as stated in the FIR.

He next submitted that as per custody certificate issued by the jail concerned, he has undergone 06 years 07 months 15 days actual imprisonment and 06 years 11 months 24 days imprisonment with remission as on 1.11.2022, thus,
he has undergone 07 years 06 months actual imprisonment and 07 years 10 months with remission till date.
Therefore, he has undergone more than half of the punishment awarded in the impugned order.

Learned counsel submits that the appeal may take some time for its final disposal and in the light of the judgement passed by Supreme Court on 25.02.2022 and 09.05.2022 in the case of Saudan Singh vs. State of U.P. in Criminal Appeal No. 308/2022 arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 4633 of 2021 and in Suleman Vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh (Misc. Application No. 764 of 2022 in Crl. Appeal No. 491 of 2022), respectively, the appellant is entitled to be released on bail.

sentences.text: The State counsel opposes the bail application and submits that although dead body of the deceased was recovered in a wheat field however, several mark of injury on the person of the deceased and cause of death was asphyxia due to ante mortem throttling.
Though on merits appellant does not have a good case but he is not in a position to dispute the detention period of the appellant.

Considering the totality of the case, in particular, detention period of the appellant and the fact that the dead body was recovered from a wheat field stained with mud and there is no eye witness of the incident, the appeal may take some time for its final disposal, without further commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the appellant on bail.

Let appellant, Ranvir @ Putan, convicted and sentenced in the above mentioned sessions trial, be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.
50,000/- (Fifty Thousand) and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
On acceptance of bail bond and personal bond, the lower court shall transmit photostat copies thereof to this Court for being kept on the record.
